title: Daniel Ernst Jablonski → Pál Ráday: draft letters on Prussian mediation in the Rákóczi war, partly in cipher, with the key sent in June 1704
correspondents: Daniel Ernst Jablonski (Prussian court preacher, Berlin) → Pál Ráday (Rákóczi's envoy, later chancellor)
shelfmark: Staatsbibliothek zu Berlin, Nachl. August Hermann Francke, 11,2/14 : 62 (24 Jun 1704, sends the key), 11,2/14 : 71 (4 Oct 1704, key not received, new key promised), 11,2/14 : 75 (8 Nov 1704, partly in cipher, decoded in some places); Briefkonzeptbuch Jablonski 1701-1704
folio_note: three drafts in Jablonski's letter-draft book; amount of cipher not known; no. 75 is the one with cipher passages left only partly decoded
status: Kalliope DE-611-HS-2910511, -2910521, -2910525 (subject 'Geheimschrift'). No. 62: 'übermittelt er den Schlüssel für eine Geheimschrift'; no. 71: recipients never got the key, copy with a new key sent via Vienna; no. 75: 'Teilweise in Geheimschrift verfaßter Text, der an einigen Stellen dekodiert ist' (partial decode). Not on DECODE (no Berlin/Wolfenbüttel holder in the repo's DECODE dumps). Not in catalogue or leads; the repo's Rákóczi targets (R483 reading) name 'domino Jablonski', so this is the Berlin end of a channel already touched.
why: Prussia's secret mediation between Rákóczi's Hungarians and Vienna in 1704, from the Berlin side, and a key that may read Ráday's received originals in Budapest.
score_note: Scored from the Kalliope descriptions during the Nov 2026 HAB/SBB sweep (research/wainut_leads_2026-11-03/); not viewed
verify: Find scans: the PRINT Migration Network (stars.library.ucf.edu, collection printmigrationnetwork-franckenachlass) hosts PDFs of single letters from these draft books; ask SBB for the 11,2/14 volume otherwise. Check Benda (ed.), Ráday Pál iratai I, 1703-1706 (Budapest 1955) for the received copies.
prior_art: unclear (checked 3 Nov 2026: repo grep, DECODE dumps, web search): Ráday's papers are edited (Benda, Ráday Pál iratai, 1955/1961), which may print the received letters in clear; drafts not checked
access_note: no SBB digitisation link in Kalliope; single letters of the Jablonski draft books are online as PDFs in the PRINT Migration Network (UCF STARS), not yet matched to these numbers
earlier_note: needs Chrome: https://digital.francke-halle.de/fshal/name/view/746123 (Francke Portal Ráday page, browser check) and https://digital.staatsbibliothek-berlin.de/suche?queryString=Briefkonzeptbuch+Jablonski (JS shell), to find a scan of SBB Francke 11,2/14. Also unopened: Benda et al., Ráday Pál iratai 1703-1706 (Budapest 1955), which would cover this exchange and was not found online (Hungaricana search 403, not on IA or REAL-EOD by what I tried). Kalliope read: no. 75 'Teilweise in Geheimschrift verfaßter Text, der an einigen Stellen dekodiert ist'; nos. 62 and 71 only discuss the key, and their records do not say they hold cipher. Key lead: Benda, Levéltári Közlemények 25 (1954), lists in the Ráday archive 44 Jablonski-Ráday letters 1704-1711 and a clavis for the Jablonski correspondence, untested. No leaf seen.

title: Daniel Ernst Jablonski → Pál Ráday: drafts with cipher written over or beside the Latin, on peace terms between Hungary and the Emperor
shelfmark: Staatsbibliothek zu Berlin, Nachl. August Hermann Francke, 11,2/15 : 8 (13 Mar 1705), 11,2/15 : 13 (18 Apr 1705), 11,2/15 : 33 (11 Sep 1705)
folio_note: nos. 8 and 13: cipher written above or parallel to the Latin text; no. 13 also discusses the encryption itself; no. 33 tagged 'Geheimschrift'
status: Kalliope DE-611-HS-2910535, -2910540, -2910560. Descriptions: 'Wortlaut teilweise mit einer Geheimschrift überschrieben'; 'teilweise parallel zum Text mit Geheimschrift geschriebenen Brief ... technische Details des Briefverkehrs, die unter anderem die Verschlüsselung betreffen'. These drafts carry the plaintext, so they are a key source rather than an open ciphertext. Not on DECODE; not in repo.
why: Plaintext-plus-cipher pairs that rebuild the Jablonski-Ráday key, which can then read cipher passages without plaintext (1704 no. 75, 1712 no. 91, and received copies in Hungary).
score_note: Scored from the Kalliope descriptions during the Nov 2026 HAB/SBB sweep (research/wainut_leads_2026-11-03/); not viewed
verify: View the 11,2/15 draft book; confirm cipher plus Latin on the same page; build the table.

Also unopened: Benda et al., Ráday Pál iratai 1703-1706 (1955). So nos. 8 and 13 should carry their Latin on the leaf and would close read if the leaf confirms it; no. 33 does not say so. Key lead: clavis for the Jablonski correspondence in the Ráday archive (Benda 1954), untested. No leaf seen.

title: Daniel Ernst Jablonski → Pál Ráday: draft wholly overwritten in cipher on the breakdown of the Hungarian-Austrian peace talks, and a follow-up
shelfmark: Staatsbibliothek zu Berlin, Nachl. August Hermann Francke, 11,2/16 : 42 (7 Dec 1706), 11,2/16 : 44 (14 Feb 1707)
folio_note: no. 42: cipher written above the Latin throughout, marked 'R I' in the margin; no. 44 tagged 'Geheimschrift'
status: Kalliope DE-611-HS-2910627, -2910629. 'über dem lateinischen Wortlaut durchweg mit Geheimschrift versehen ... am Rand mit R I gezeichnet' (a second key, 'R I'?). Content: Ilgen and Frederick I on the Jesuit-driven break-off of the talks; Spanish Succession and Great Northern War diplomacy. Not on DECODE; not in repo.
why: Full cipher-over-plaintext draft; the 'R I' mark suggests a numbered key, useful against other Rákóczi-side Berlin traffic.

title: Daniel Ernst Jablonski → Francis II Rákóczi: news from M. Klement at The Hague and of Prince Eugene's journey to England, partly in cipher
correspondents: Daniel Ernst Jablonski → Francis II Rákóczi
shelfmark: Staatsbibliothek zu Berlin, Nachl. August Hermann Francke, 11,2/17 : 91 (Briefkonzeptbuch Jablonski 1711-1712)
folio_note: one draft, '[Teilweise mit Geheimschrift]'; extent unknown
status: Kalliope DE-611-HS-2910745. Draft; no decipherment noted. Same volume holds Jablonski → Rákóczi 26 Sep 1711 (11,2/17 : 58), which is online as a PDF in the PRINT Migration Network (UCF STARS item 66), so this draft book has been imaged. Rákóczi ciphers are in the repo (R483 etc.); not on DECODE as a Berlin item.
why: Rákóczi in exile after Szatmár (1711) and his Hague agent Klement; could tie the Berlin cipher to the Rákóczi keys already rebuilt.

why: Grebner's political prophecies (the 'Seidenfaden') circulated widely; a cipher section of nine leaves may hold a hidden version.
